change.before: The \ac{sg} of Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} keeps the structural skeleton of Definition~\ref{def:relu_net_game}: per-neuron $\pm$ states, stop-versus-continue actions, the bias as continuation payoff and the input as final payoff, the transition kernel \eqref{eq:rng_kernel} driven by the weight parts $\Wsig{l}{\sigma}$, the cemetery state, and the structural discounts $\gamma^{(l)}_i$. Two changes are load-bearing for attribution. First, the original tracks only the single signed value \eqref{eq:rng_value_identity}; Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} additionally maintains a \emph{non-negative payoff per player}, identifying the pair of player-specific values $\Vp{p}{s}$, $p \in \{+,-\}$, with the two streams of the Stopping Decomposition of Section~\ref{sec:stopping_decomposition} and recovering \eqref{eq:rng_value_identity} as their difference. Second, the signed terminal payoffs $\xi_q\, x_k$ become the non-negative pair $(x_k^{+}, x_k^{-})$ of Definition~\ref{def:posneg_parts}, keeping every player-specific quantity non-negative and exposing the parity structure of backward trajectories. Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} further extends the graph to skip connections and max-pooling and adds risk aversion and regularized policies, none of which appear in the original game.
change.after: The \ac{sg} retains Definition~\ref{def:relu_net_game}'s per-neuron $\pm$ states, stop/continue actions, bias and terminal input payoffs, weight-part kernel \eqref{eq:rng_kernel}, cemetery, and structural discounts $\gamma^{(l)}_i$. Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} adds \emph{non-negative player payoffs}: the values $\Vp{p}{s}$, $p\in\{+,-\}$, equal the Stopping Decomposition streams (Section~\ref{sec:stopping_decomposition}), whose difference recovers the original signed value \eqref{eq:rng_value_identity}. Replacing signed terminal payoffs $\xi_qx_k$ by $(x_k^+,x_k^-)$ (Definition~\ref{def:posneg_parts}) keeps all player-specific quantities non-negative and exposes backward-trajectory parity. The chapter also adds skip connections, max-pooling, risk aversion, and regularized policies, absent from the original game.
